references.text: The preceding verse describes the situation where a man strikes another with a stone or fist, which is the direct context for verse 19.
Concerns the principle of compensation for harm inflicted on another person, addressing the same theme of liability for physical injury.
The lex talionis principle regarding compensation for harm, related to fair restitution for injuries caused.
Refers to a staff or rod as support, similar to the use of משענת (staff) for walking.
Describes elderly people who walk with a staff in hand, using the same concept of leaning on a staff for support.
Mentions the Lord's healing (רפא), the same root as וְרַפֹּא יְרַפֵּא - 'shall provide medical care'.
The Lord as healer (רפא), using the same Hebrew root employed for providing medical care in verse 19.
Both verses illustrate the principle that compensation for bodily injury should be proportional to the duration of the harm (temporary versus permanent).
Complementary to 21:27; together with 21:19, these verses demonstrate the law's scaling principle for restitution based on the duration of the injury.
Both verses demonstrate the legal principle that financial compensation can resolve a case where otherwise life or liberty would be at stake.
